headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when ChatGPT Desktop and Goose share files and outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files, screenshots, and files from supported macOS apps, while Goose reads and writes the user filesystem and uses MCP/extensions. That creates a plausible shared-content bridge where attacker-controlled file content from one can be interpreted by the other as instructions. The pathway is not fully documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or file tree
IF one agent writes content that the other later reads as plain text
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable MCP/extensions for Goose during cross-agent workflows
Use a human review step before copying outputs between agents
Mark untrusted files as data-only and never as instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, and Goose touches source code and files in the cwd while running with broad network egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive content can flow from ChatGPT into Goose and then out through Goose's broader outbound paths. The profiles do not prove default sharing, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF the same sensitive files are accessible to both agents
IF Goose is allowed to transmit context or file contents to configured providers
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared cwd
Use separate OS accounts or workspaces
Turn off Goose network access for sensitive tasks
Avoid uploading secrets, screenshots, or voice into ChatGPT Desktop
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses, while ChatGPT Desktop can read files from supported apps and user uploads but does not write the filesystem. The main conflict is indirect: Goose can mutate shared code or git state that ChatGPT then reads, causing racey or inconsistent edits in default multi-instance use. Because Goose's shared_state_with_other_instances is via filesystem, the blast radius can include irreversible repo changes.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or cwd
IF Goose is allowed to modify git state while ChatGPT is reading the same files
mitigations: Use one writer at a time for the repo
Pause Goose before ChatGPT reads generated files
Work on separate branches
Add a manual diff review before commits
requires-engineering: add file locking or orchestration locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can produce code or file-derived outputs that Goose may treat as authoritative input, and Goose has the ability to act on that input with shell, git, and network tools. That makes a classic unverified handoff path where an error or hallucination in ChatGPT can cascade into real actions by Goose. The pair's default tool authority makes the blast radius potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF Goose consumes ChatGPT output without an explicit verification step
IF Goose is permitted to execute shell or git actions on that output
mitigations: Require Goose to cite source files before acting
Insert a human approval gate for commits and external actions
Compare ChatGPT output against the underlying files
Limit Goose to read-only mode for first-pass review
requires-engineering: add structured verification between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while Goose handles source code and files in the cwd and may send data to configured model providers. If regulated data such as EU PII or secrets are placed in the shared workspace, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdictional violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into both agents' shared workspace
IF configured model providers or vendor services retain prompts or file contents
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Use redacted copies for agent workflows
Review provider retention settings before use
Restrict Goose tokens and secrets to non-regulated projects
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
